worked_solution:
First, from the equation of the plane we get that the normal vector of $Π$ is $n=⟨3,1,2⟩.$

Now, we solve the Cartesian equation of $Π$ for $z$:

$$
\begin{aligned}3x+y+2z+4 & =0 \\ 2z & =-3x-y-4 \\ z & =-\frac{3}{2}x-\frac{1}{2}y-2\end{aligned}
$$

If we put $x=0$ and $y=0$, we get $z=-2.$ Hence, the point $P(0,0,-2)$ lies on $Π.$ Note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨0,0,-2⟩.$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ (r-⟨0,0,-2⟩)\cdot ⟨3,1,2⟩ & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
